connections.name: Larry Ellison
connections.description: Disputed. Haaretz reported in September 2021 that Ellison offered Netanyahu a seat on Oracle's board; Netanyahu denied receiving the offer and Oracle declined to comment. In August 2021 Netanyahu dined with Ellison in Hawaii while Ellison was listed as a state's witness in Netanyahu's corruption trial.

sources.title: Larry Ellison Offers Netanyahu Lucrative Oracle Post — Haaretz
Benjamin Netanyahu dines with state's witness against him in Hawaii — The Jerusalem Post

connections.name: Miriam Adelson
connections.description: The Adelsons were early backers of Netanyahu in 1996, and Israel Hayom has been widely seen as favoring him. They fell out after Israel's attorney general alleged in 2017 that Netanyahu sought a deal with a rival paper's publisher, and by about 2019 had cut off contact with him and his wife.

sources.title: Adelson: Sara Netanyahu said if Israel is destroyed it'll be my fault — Jerusalem Post

connections.name: Yoram Hazony
connections.description: In the early 1990s Hazony worked as an aide to then-opposition leader Netanyahu, attending the Madrid peace talks with him and helping with two of his books.

name: Benjamin Netanyahu

lean.basis: Leader of the right-wing Likud since 1993 (with a break) and prime minister at the head of right-wing coalitions; made his closeness to Donald Trump central to his appeal.

current_role: Prime Minister of Israel (caretaker after the October 27, 2026 election; see source conflicts)
summary: Benjamin Netanyahu is Israel's longest-serving prime minister (1996–1999, 2009–2021 and since 2022). A former special-forces soldier and UN ambassador, he has led Likud since 1993 with a break, and built his politics around close ties to Donald Trump. Yoram Hazony was his aide in the early 1990s; the Adelsons were early backers. The October 2026 election left his bloc short of a majority.

sources.title: Right-wing bloc wins Israeli election with 53 seats — JNS

source_conflicts.details: Wikipedia says he lost and is set to be replaced by Gadi Eisenkot on November 8, 2026; late-October reporting found his bloc ahead (53 seats to 48) but short of a majority, with both sides claiming a mandate and no government formed.

sources.title: Right-wing bloc wins Israeli election with 53 seats — JNS
Israel elections: Netanyahu, Eisenkot each claim mandate after tight vote — Khaleej Times
